q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer — the data does not agree with your premise: net ROAS fell to 0.86x while order‑date net profit was negative (₹-6,921) for 2026-09-30..2026-10-13; the diagnostic engine found no single supported cause and judged the moves within recent variation.  

Evidence (Measured)
- Net ROAS (order-date): prior ≈ 0.92x → current 0.86x. — Measured  
- Net profit (order-date): current = ₹-6,921. — Measured  
- Net profit, recent normal days: median = ₹5,158; range = ₹-12,846 → ₹26,973. — Measured (daily net profit series)  
- Key components: contribution margin ₹562,162 → ₹648,034 (+15.0%); ad spend ₹610,468 → ₹744,922 (+22.0%). — Measured  
- Lever highlights: ad spend per order ₹946.7 → ₹1,203 (+27%) which moved Net ROAS down (~-21.3%); contribution margin per order ↑(+8%) which moved Net ROAS up (~+7.9%); CPA / cost-per-order rose (~+58%) even as CPC/CPM fell, so spend bought volume but at weaker profit per order. — Measured

Interpretation
- Measured: higher ad spend and higher cost per converted order outpaced contribution improvements, producing lower ROAS on the lever ladder and a decline in net profit.  
- Hypothesis: mix and allocation shifts (which campaigns/products the spend went to) likely explain why volume rose but profitability fell — the diagnostic run found mix shifts but no single statistically supported upstream cause.

Period: 2026-09-30..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
